subject: Clarify: Packaging surcharge & caps in Order Form (Exhibit A/B)
messages:
From: Aditi Menon <aditi.menon@quantum-retail.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@quantum-retail.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging surcharge in Exhibit B — need clarity

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the call earlier. We reviewed the draft Order Form and have a couple of procurement questions before we can move to internal legal: the new "packaging surcharge" in Exhibit B (section 2.3) looks like a pass-through but the language references both a per-SKU uplift and a quarterly reconciliation cap. Can you confirm:

- Is the surcharge intended to be additive to the per-token/seat pricing, or is it meant to replace certain line items?
- What exactly triggers the quarterly cap? (cumulative surcharge across SKUs vs per-SKU ceiling)
- Is there an example calculation you can share for a 3-month billing window with tiered seats?

Also, your side flagged an annual cap/floor that interacts with our committed minimums — procurement wants to be sure we won't be double-assessed when the true-up runs. We attached our annotated copy (see Exhibit-A_PricingSchedule_QRT_v3.pdf).

We need these clarifications to finish our redline and get to signature.

Best,
Aditi
Procurement — Quantum Retail Technologies

Attachment: Exhibit-A_PricingSchedule_QRT_v3.pdf (pdf, 92KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Menon <aditi.menon@quantum-retail.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@quantum-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging surcharge in Exhibit B — need clarity

Aditi — thanks for the clear note. High level answers below and I attached a trackers-friendly redline for Exhibit B.

- Packaging surcharge is additive to listed unit pricing (per-inference SKU lines). It's a line-level uplift intended to capture variable packaging costs (carrier/format-specific) that don't fit standard token/seat pricing.
- The quarterly "surcharge cap" we proposed is a single aggregate cap across all SKUs for the invoice period (i.e., the sum of surcharges from all SKUs cannot exceed the cap). We can change that to a per-SKU cap if you prefer — see option B in the redline.
- Example calculation (simple):
  * Base unit charge = $0.004 per inference token; packaging surcharge = $0.0005 per token for compressed-binary bundles; total = $0.0045 per token.
  * Quarterly reconciliation: if total billed surcharge > quarterly cap, excess is refunded as a credit on next invoice; if billed surcharge < floor, Redwood issues a credit to reach the floor (this floor is to guarantee minimum pass-through coverage).

On the double-assessment concern with committed minimums: the surcharge is excluded from the committed-usage true-up. The Exhibit language should be explicit: "surcharge amounts are excluded from committed-usage calculations and true-up." I asked Legal (Neha) to review wording — looping her in.

I've attached: redline-ExhibitB-packaging-surcharge-track-changes.docx showing option A (aggregate cap) and option B (per-SKU cap), and a short worked example in the footnote.

Next steps: pick cap model (aggregate or per-SKU) and confirm whether the surcharge should appear as a separate invoice line or bundled into the unit price. We can provide a short amendment if you want the cap to be temporary for the first contract year.

Cheers,
Priyom
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-ExhibitB-packaging-surcharge-track-changes.docx (docx, 34KB)

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@quantum-retail.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Aditi Menon <aditi.menon@quantum-retail.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-01T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging surcharge in Exhibit B — need clarity

Thanks — useful. Quick clarifying notes from procurement: we prefer the per-SKU cap (Option B) because different SKUs have materially different packaging profiles (edge vs batch bundles). Two asks before we hand to our legal:

1) Please strike the floor wording that suggests Redwood may "issue a credit to reach the floor" — procurement is worried that a guaranteed floor could be interpreted as an additional fixed charge if volumes fall. Can you instead make it a "surcharge smoothing buffer" where Redwood may credit back only if actual pass-through costs exceed the billed surcharge?

2) We want the surcharge excluded from the committed minimum (great that you confirmed). Please add a short definitional sentence: "For avoidance of doubt, packaging surcharge shall not count toward Customer Commitments defined in Section X."

If Legal is aligned, we can send a single consolidated redline. Rajiv

Subject: Re: Packaging surcharge in Exhibit B — need clarity (legal redline suggestion)

Team / Aditi — thanks for the flags. Quick legal proposal below that preserves Redwood's cost recovery and addresses procurement's concern about a hard floor. I've included the suggested text to paste into Exhibit B (track-changes version attached).

Proposed exhibit language (suggested insertion in Section 2.3):
"Packaging Surcharge. Customer will be billed a packaging surcharge calculated per applicable SKU as set forth on the Pricing Schedule. For each calendar quarter, Redwood will apply a cap to the total packaging surcharge billed to the Customer (the "Quarterly Packaging Cap"). Any surcharge amounts billed in excess of the Quarterly Packaging Cap will be credited to Customer on the next invoice. For the first contract year only, Redwood will offer a surcharge smoothing buffer (the "Smoothing Buffer") designed to reduce billing volatility: if actual pass-through packaging costs materially exceed the billed surcharge for the quarter (as demonstrated by reasonable supporting invoices), Redwood will credit Customer up to the amount of the Smoothing Buffer. The Smoothing Buffer is not a minimum guaranteed charge and shall not be considered a fee for any purpose."

Key points implemented:
- Per-SKU cap option incorporated (meets procurement preference).
- Eliminated language that could be read as a fixed minimum; replaced with a conditional Smoothing Buffer (first-year only) that is explicitly not a guaranteed charge.
- Added explicit exclusion from Commitments (see definitional sentence): "For avoidance of doubt, packaging surcharge and any credits or adjustments related thereto shall not count toward Customer Commitments or committed usage calculations."

If that language is acceptable, I'll produce a clean track-changes doc and we can proceed to a single consolidated Order Form redline for signature. Also confirm whether Quantum wants the surcharge as a separate invoice line (preferred for transparency) — if so, we'll update Exhibit A formatting.

Neha Kapoor
Associate Counsel — Redwood Inference
